key_insight: Real coding-agent usage is dominated by long autonomous loops with long contexts, short outputs, and highly variable tool-call patterns, which makes LLM serving behavior very different from standard chat workloads.
engineering_relevance: Serving systems for coding agents should optimize for low-overhead tool calls, append-length-aware prefill, smarter tool-latency prediction, and KV-cache policies that handle human-paced gaps.
method: Collected ~4,300 real coding-agent sessions from day-to-day use of Claude Code and Codex.
Logged ~350,000 LLM steps and ~430,000 tool calls for workload analysis.
Analyzed context length, output length, tool-call diversity, and prefix-cache behavior to identify serving bottlenecks.
evidence_signal: The trace dataset spans roughly 4,300 sessions and supports analysis of about 350,000 LLM steps and 430,000 tool calls, revealing high but imperfect prefix-cache hit rates.
watch_item: The trace reflects the authors' own day-to-day usage, so patterns may not fully generalize to all coding-agent users, orgs, or model configurations.
paper_title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
